scenes.title: The Lantern Writ, read on Market Square

beats.speaker: herald
beats.text: Hear the old King's writ. Should I go up with no word given, the work of reigning passes to the wolf who keeps the peace of the Sump.

beats.speaker: herald
beats.text: To hold until the realm howls a Moot: the nine voices of the communities, the four Houses in Council, and the free wolves of the roads.

beats.speaker: herald
beats.text: That is the writ. It was found by a wolf of this realm, and it is the law.

beats.speaker: captain
beats.text: I barred the mine house in the deep winter. The Deepvein wolves knocked till morning, eh. I counted the knocks.

beats.speaker: keeper
beats.text: Lamp's thanks for saying it. Late, but said.

beats.speaker: skipper
beats.text: Hold it, hold it. There. Green as a pike and loud as a gale, eh. Mirebridge's bell.

beats.speaker: skipper
beats.text: Five winters under the ice, and it still knows how to ring. Calm water, all of you.

Hilde (paid), the Speaker, and Desmond Hollis (unless he fled) tell what they saw in their windows.
One memory a witness, to the first wolf (the race, nh_witnesses_heard): 4 points; the 23rd opens the search.

effect.detail: heard what the Chancellor wept over

effect.text: They remember the day: the month before the old King went up, a wet morning, the Rain Hall's lamps lit at noon.
They remember the seal on the paper: the old King's own, the lamp and the crown, pressed deep.
They remember who stood beside him: a Counting House clerk, who took the paper back when the weeping stopped.
They remember which way he walked after: not home, but to the City Office, with the paper under his coat.
Someone has already heard this memory. Another witness, then.

triggers.note: At 23 memories the search opens (and Hilde's race begins: ten game days for someone to face the Chancellor).

effect.text: Twenty-three wolves of the city saw the Chancellor weep over a paper with the old King's seal. Where did the paper go? The Records Office rolls, the cathedral crypt, the Greatly Bank: somebody should look.
Twenty-three memories, and they agree: a paper with the old King's seal. The search for it is open.

triggers.note: Hilde's Whisper: ten pennies, and she remembers (her pair key opens her window's choice).

Ten game days after the 23rd memory with no confrontation: Hilde gets there first, the Chancellor pays her; the writ, if not yet found, may move to another site, never to one already searched (it stays put when the draw falls on one).

effect.text: Hilde Dripby was at the City Office door before any of you. The Chancellor paid her, and says nothing now.
The paper has been moved, they say. Wherever you looked before, look again.

triggers.note: Confronting the Chancellor (three testimonies heard): each wolf's answer, once; the first to a majority decides.

effect.text: He will not hear it from you: three wolves' memories at least, and only once.

triggers.note: The Chancellor's fate: the first answer held by a majority of the wolves who faced him.

effect.reason: The Chancellor told the Council of the Counting House's order to lose the old King's writ.

effect.text: The Chancellor has stood before the Council of Houses and told it: the old King's writ, the debt the Counting House held, and the order to lose it. He keeps his post, and his eyes on the floor.
PRINTED BY THE COUNCIL PRESS: a note in the Counting House's own paw to the Chancellor. "Lose it, and your note is torn."

triggers.note: A site searched: the writ if it is there; otherwise what that site holds (campaign Ch 8, the Search).

effect.text: In the rolls: the Council's order striking Mirebridge from them five winters ago, sealed by the Houses' seats. Not the writ, but the scattered will want to know.
Behind the abbot's stone: the old King's own draft of the lamp-book line, in his paw. Not the writ, but the herald could read it at the Moot.
In the strongbox under the flat's boards: a note to the Chancellor. "Lose it, and your note is torn." The Counting House's own paw.

triggers.note: A Records Office clerk asked to go through the old rolls (five askings in all, by any wolves).
The Lantern Writ found: it goes to the finder (a story item), the herald reads it at noon.

effect.text: #thanks#. You found it. I will read it at noon on Market Square, every word, and I will say who found it.
THE LANTERN WRIT IS FOUND. The herald reads it at noon on Market Square. (signed) The Herald of Ridgemere
The Lantern Writ is found. The herald will read it at noon on Market Square.

effect.text: The Counting House is short of coin this week: the clerk counts you out two loaves instead.

triggers.note: Noon after the writ is found: the herald reads it on Market Square (a public scene; the same words on every board).

triggers.note: Six bearings place the bell; the bell placed and the frame given: the haul runs from the next dusk.

effect.text: SIX BEARINGS ON THE ICE, AND THE BELL IS PLACED. Timber, tug ropes and rope to the skipper at Upper Mere for the frame. (signed) The skipper at Upper Mere
Six bearings cross on the Upper Mere. The bell lies under them.
THE HAUL BEGINS AT DUSK on the Upper Mere. Bring a tug rope, take a rope from the skipper, and pull when he says. Not before. (signed) The skipper at Upper Mere
The frame stands over the bell. The haul begins at dusk: a tug rope, a rope from Kell, and every back you can bring.

triggers.note: Hakon on the Pass road at night; on a Restday, the mine captain to the Lamp and Pick if asked; a haul dusk: the hands on the ropes (wolves who took a rope this dusk and carry a tug rope, Kell, and Coldwater's folk).

effect.name: a grey-cloaked wolf from over the Pass
effect.description: a lean wolf in a grey cloak, smelling of old smoke, who will not say his name

effect.text: The mine captain is walking down to the Lamp and Pick, with the valley in to drink. Whoever wants to hear him should be at its door.

triggers.note: Enough hands, max(4, helpers / 8): a good dusk; three good (two with the pup taught) raise it; two bad crack it.

effect.text: A good pull. The bell came a length up the frame.
A good pull. The bell stirred in the mud and came a length up the frame.
Too few hands on the ropes. The bell slid back, and something in it rang flat.

triggers.note: The bell raised (rung): Mirebridge +20, the scene at the shore, every hauler thanked; a close held for the haul goes now.

effect.text: From the north-east, over the snow, a bell no living wolf has heard.

effect.detail: hauled the drowned bell from under the Upper Mere ice

effect.text: #thanks#, #address#. You pulled when I said, and not before. The mere gave it back.

triggers.note: Two failed dusks: the bell comes up cracked (Mirebridge +10); a close held for the haul goes now.

effect.text: The bell is up, but it rings flat: a crack from lip to crown. It goes to the city all the same. (signed) The skipper at Upper Mere
The bell came up at last, cracked from lip to crown. It rings flat, but it rings.

triggers.note: Ask the mine captain to say it at the Lamp and Pick (the list read first): asked any day, he walks there on the next Restday at nightfall (on a Restday he may be anywhere, and his house is his home).

triggers.note: The mine captain at the door: he says it if someone is there to hear (two, if his seam note was crooked).

effect.text: The mine captain stood at the Lamp and Pick door, and nobody was there to hear it. He went back up to the mine. He will come again next Restday.

triggers.note: The confession said: Frosthollow knows; Ulric walks up the Pass road to look for his brother (and comes back at dawn); the mine captain goes back up to the mine.

effects.text: It's moving again, eh. I heard it ring under my paws.
THE MERE IS SKINNING OVER. Wolves with ropes and strong backs, to the Upper Mere when it freezes. (signed) The skipper at Upper Mere
A grey paw-mark, pressed in lamp-black, and under it: ON THE MOOT NIGHT THE PASS IS MINE.

quests.title: Hilde's Whisper
quests.summary: Hilde Dripby of the Rag Mill saw the Chancellor weep in the Rain Hall, and sells what she saw. She drinks at the Drowned Lantern after work. Ten pennies, she says, and she will remember something.

objectives.label: Give Hilde Dripby ten pennies, in her window.
Ask her what she saw.

rewards.text: He wept in the Rain Hall the month before the old King went up, over a paper. Hilde is not the only one who saw it. Ask the others, kindly.

quests.title: The Chancellor Wept
quests.summary: Forty-odd wolves of the city once saw the Chancellor weep in the Rain Hall and have told no one. Each will tell the first wolf who is kind to them: a gift, or a meal shared. Three memories, and you could put it to the Chancellor himself.

objectives.label: Hear three memories of the weeping from those who saw it.

quests.title: The Search for the Writ
quests.summary: The paper the Chancellor wept over is somewhere: the Records Office rolls, the cathedral crypt behind the abbot's stone, or the flat over the Greatly Bank. Search all three if you must.

objectives.label: Ask the Records Office clerks to go through the old rolls with you (five askings).
Ask the abbot, at the cathedral, for leave to look behind his stone in the crypt.
Go down to the crypt at night and look behind the abbot's stone.
Ask the moneychanger at the Greatly Bank to let you look in her flat.
Find the Lantern Writ.

quests.title: The Old Wolves of the Bilge
quests.summary: The Sump's oldest drink at the Bilge and the Knucklebones of an evening. Share a meal with three of them and they will give you the old King's own saying, for the herald.

objectives.label: Share a meal with three of the Sump's elders, at the Bilge or the Knucklebones.

rewards.detail: ate with the old wolves of the Bilge and brought back the old King's saying

rewards.text: The old King used to say it on the Sump Stairs: the Sump keeps its own peace, or nobody does.

quests.title: A Visit to the Cells
quests.summary: Desmond Hollis was on the Rain Hall door the day the Chancellor wept. He is in the Keep's cells now. Go down, bring him something, and ask him.

objectives.label: Bring Desmond Hollis a kindness in the cells, and hear what he saw at the Rain Hall door.

quests.title: Kell's Winter
quests.summary: Kell Greyton, skipper at Upper Mere, heard something ring under the ice, and he does not trust the city. Fish the mere with him, bring his coat some fur oil, and he will lead the bearings.

objectives.label: Take a duck on the Upper Mere.
Give Kell a fur oil for his coat.

rewards.detail: fished the Upper Mere with its skipper

quests.title: The Bell's Frame
quests.summary: A frame over the bell, and no project to build it: Kell needs eight timber, four tug ropes and six rope, and Willa's cart to bring the frame timber from Coldwater.

offer.say: #greet#. A frame over the bell, and strong. Eight of timber, four tug ropes and six of rope, and Willa's cart from Coldwater with the long beams. Bring it, and we haul, eh?
offer.accept: I will bring what I can.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. That is a frame, eh. Now we wait for dusk, and we pull together.

objectives.label: Give Kell eight of timber.
Give Kell four tug ropes.
Give Kell six of rope.
Walk Willa's cart from Coldwater to the Upper Mere boat shed.

rewards.detail: raised the frame over the drowned bell

quests.title: Stillwater Lessons
quests.summary: The Reedmere pup at the Glasswater landing hums, and the water listens. Teach her slowly, as Kell says: time spent with her, a song at the landing, humming with her when the ice is restless.

objectives.label: Give the pup ten lessons, between you.

rewards.detail: sat with the Reedmere pup while the water went still

quests.title: The Lamp-Oil List
quests.summary: Frosthollow's record of the deep winters has a list of who shared their lamp oil, and no Deepvein name on it. Read it to Ulric. Then bring the mine captain to the Lamp and Pick on a Restday evening, and let him say it in front of the valley.

objectives.label: Tell Ulric Stonevein there is no Deepvein name on the lamp-oil list.
Ask the mine captain to come and say it at the Lamp and Pick. He walks there at nightfall on a Restday.
Be at the Lamp and Pick door when he says it.

rewards.detail: heard the mine captain say what he barred in the deep winter

quests.title: The Frosthollow Count
quests.summary: Iron for the bell's yoke, from the Frosthollow mine. Nobody goes down alone, and nobody comes up without counting the others.

objectives.label: Go to the mine mouth in a party of two or more.
Give Kell four of iron ore for the yoke.

rewards.detail: went down the Frosthollow mine for the bell's yoke, and counted everyone up

quests.title: Gorse on the Ice
quests.summary: Gorse Reedmere keeps creeping out on the ice to watch the black lane. Find him out there and walk him home to the landing.

objectives.label: Find Gorse out on the Upper Mere ice.
Walk him home to the Glasswater landing.

rewards.detail: walked the Reedmere pup home off the ice

quests.title: Feed Larkfield
quests.summary: The ford burned and Larkfield's harvest with it. Bread, flour, oats or fish to Larkfield's folk, three times.

objectives.label: Give food to Larkfield's folk, in Larkfield (three gifts).

rewards.detail: fed Larkfield after the ford burned

tests.name: Good roads: writ read, Chancellor confesses, Queen fights, pup taught, bell rung; ready day 24
Worse roads: exposed, writ sold, bell cracked, pup pledged; Advance anyway waits out the haul
Pup hidden and found, Chancellor flees, Queen accepts, no haul: the bell lost
Hilde first: he pays her after ten days; the writ never moves to a searched site; pup hidden
One active wolf (winter: no freeze) is the floor; ready day 24; the bar short
Readiness, five active wolves: 30% and the floor of 3, after 24 days
Readiness, 200 active wolves: 60 of them (30%) must have done a task
Advance anyway before the minimum time: day 2, nobody has done a task
Soft maximum, auto off: past 60 days with too few, it waits for the admin
The soft maximum with auto on: past 60 days it moves by itself
Waiting for the bar: three took part after 24 days; it waits until the bar is full
